A summary of the meeting notes is presented: NREL presented the idea of the combined CVD-Fz process to the engineers at PVATepla. PVATepla expressed that there would be challenges with incorporating CVD into a Float Zone crystallizer but also that they though the idea was exciting and technically feasible on its face. They confirmed that their crystallizers could operate at elevated pressures up to 6 bar (absolute), validating our choice to model growth at this pressure. PVATepla emphasized the need to keep reactants out of the crystallization zone, and that presently the max Argon flow possible for protection was 20 standard liters per minute, which helped inform our modeling. They also confirmed that the present maximum boule size of float zone crystallizers is 8” and that challenges with stabilizing the liquid melt would have to be overcome to move to Page 25 of 30 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. larger sizes. They were not sure if the RF heating limited the 8” boule or not. PVATepla expressed possible interest in a future collaboration on a system if external funding could be obtained. Mark Loboda of Hemlock Semiconductor also reviewed and signed off on the report. Overall, Mark is optimistic in the outlook for the technology. Mark sees potential for these crystallizers to be more automated than the Siemens process presently is, providing a competitive advantage for the technology. Mark’s largest concern was the expectation of heterogeneous Si deposits on internal surfaces of the reactor. It will be important to incorporate cooling for internal surfaces to ensure that the TCS does not crack and deposit Si on these surfaces, but only on the boule. This effect could place a lower limit on the width of the growth channel, to prevent too much accumulation of deposits and choking of this inlet. The optimization of the design, technoeconomic analysis, and presentation of the results to potential industrial partners complete milestone 1.1.5. 8. Significant Accomplishments and Conclusions: The modeling effort proved that it is possible to operate the reactor in a way that generates a high growth rate above 100 µm/min while keeping the crystallization region of the chamber clean of TCS. Using this growth rate, the technoeconomic analysis suggests that Fz Si wafers can be produced with a levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) that is lower than the incumbent technology of Siemens + Cz crystallization.
